transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-04-22
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 42m
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Claire Atkins (Redwood CS); Elena Ruiz (TerraFlux Head of ML), Jon Park (Platform Eng), Priya Menon (VP Finance), Amit Rao (Security)

Summary:
TerraFlux confirmed intention to renew current contract and add a reserved Dedicated capacity top-up for EU region. Primary drivers: latency-sensitive user flows in EU, data residency for EU PII, predictable unit economics for high-volume inference. Open items: finalize pricing amendment, share SOC2 + KMS details, run a performance benchmark on dedicated pool, align on cutover plan and pilot timeline.

Topics:
1) Current usage profile & growth forecast
2) Dedicated vs Hosted for EU flows (latency / cost tradeoff)
3) Security and data residency (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
4) Timeline & commercial amendment

Action items (short list in transcript): Maya to send amendment, Samir to design benchmark, Amit to share compliance doc, Jon to send traffic curves.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right everyone thanks for joining. Uh this is Maya from Redwood, i'm here with Samir our solutions engineer and Claire from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Elena: Good thanks, thanks Maya. Busy week but excited to get this moving.
[00:12] Jon: Hi all, quick note - i'm on mobile so audio might be iffy.
[00:16] Maya: Totally fine. Quick agenda: we wanted to confirm TerraFlux's renewal intent, talk capacity top-up for EU, run through security asks and next steps. Does that align?
[00:25] Priya: Yes, sounds good. From finance side we just need clarity on the amendment numbers and confirmation of start date for the committed capacity.
[00:33] Amit: And from security, SOC2 and KMS integration are blockers until we see docs. Also need to know whether audit logs and RBAC export is on the plan.
[00:42] Samir: Got it. We'll cover the KMS options and audit log retention in the doc. On the infra side, quick q: Jon, can you remind us of the percentage of requests hitting EU endpoints today?
[00:52] Jon: Roughly 28% of traffic is EU, but it's spiky during peak hours. 99th pct for EU routes is around 820ms right now, which is borderline for some flows. We saw a few timeouts in last month's run.
[01:05] Elena: Yeah the latency spike is our biggest concern - user-facing token-generation for chat needs to be under 500ms 99th ideally.
[01:12] Maya: Thanks, that's really helpful. So two levers: we can route EU traffic to hosted EU models (lower ops) or provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west to hit lower latency and predictable throughput. Dedicated will give you reserved GPU pools, predictable 99th, and a per-month commitment.
[01:30] Priya: From finance perspective what's the delta between hosted cost and Dedicated committed rate? Ballpark is fine.
[01:36] Samir: Ballpark: if you're talking about sustained QPS at your scale, Dedicated can be about 35-45% cheaper per token once you amortize commit, depending on batching and KV cache effectiveness. But up-front is the commitment.
[01:50] Priya: Ok that helps. We need a clear example with their current qps.
[01:54] Jon: i'll share the qps and token distribution after the call.
[01:58] Maya: Perfect. On the security front, Amit are you looking for customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed?
[02:04] Amit: Prefer customer-managed KMS for the private deployment. For hosted EU we can accept Redwood KMS if we get attestations and HSM notes. Also need to know key rotation and delete workflows.
[02:15] Claire: We can share the KMS integration spec and the HSM attestation doc. For Private deployments we support customer KMS via standard KMS providers, and we have an HSM flow for dedicated appliances.
[02:27] Amit: Great. Also RBAC -- need role separation and audit logs exported to our SIEM; we'll need S3 or syslog endpoint support.
[02:35] Samir: Yes we have audit logs export, and syslog is supported. We'll add examples in the onboarding runbook.
[02:41] [crosstalk] Elena: Oh and data residency - the PII redaction question was raised by legal. Do you offer automatic redaction?
[02:48] Samir: We have optional PII redaction hooks that run pre-ingest and post-response; they're configurable. We'll include the doc.
[02:55] Maya: Quick note on rollout: our recommended approach is a pilot on Dedicated in eu-west with a small slice of traffic (5-10%), run perf tests and then a staged cutover. That keeps risk low.
[03:07] Jon: What's the pilot duration you're seeing as typical?
[03:11] Samir: Usually 2 weeks of steady-state plus a 1-week stress test. That gives us reliable lat/throughput curves.
[03:19] Priya: For contracting, can you send an amendment that shows current term, new EU capacity line item and the start date? We want to avoid a full multi-year recommit if possible.
[03:29] Maya: We can draft a 12-month amendment with an option to convert to longer term at renewal - i'll include pricing tiers for burst and sustained usage.
[03:36] Priya: That would be ideal.
[03:38] Elena: Are there any capacity pre-warm or provisioning windows we should expect? Last time we saw a 48 hour provisioning lag.
[03:44] Samir: For Dedicated reserved pools we provision within 24-72 hours depending on stock in region, but we can offer short-term bursts if you need immediate capacity while dedicated is stood up.
[03:53] Jon: Good to know. One more technical: does Redwood's runtime support our multi-model routing? We sometimes route small prompts to a distilled model and long contexts to the larger model.
[04:03] Samir: Yes, routing by model variant is supported. You can pin per-route model versions, and we automatically fallback to compatible variants if the primary isn't available. There might be small matching issues in auto-fallback naming; i think you mentioned the KV cache behavior earlier?
[04:16] Elena: Yeah we rely on persistent KV cache for chat sessions - will that survive model switch?
[04:20] Samir: It does for compatible architecture; we'll call out incompatibilities in the runbook. Sometimes the transcriber shows 'KV cash' in docs, haha, but realistically it's KV cache.
[04:30] [laughs]
[04:33] Maya: Ok circling back to next steps. jon to share traffic curves, Amit to share compliance matrix, Samir will prepare benchmark plan, and I will draft the amendment and share pricing. Any other blockers?
[04:44] Priya: One ask from procurement is a sample SLA for regional deployments, specifically 99th pct latency targets and credits.
[04:51] Maya: We'll include target SLOs in the amendment and a separate SLA appendix for eu-west.
[04:57] Elena: timeline wise we need the amendment and security docs within this week to get internal sign-off.
[05:03] Maya: Understood. We'll aim to send amendment by Friday 2025-04-25.
[05:07] Jon: i'll try to turn around traffic exports by tomorrow.
[05:10] Amit: i'll compile the SOC2 and compliance gap by Tuesday.
[05:14] Samir: I'll prepare the perf plan and sample prompts, target delivery 2025-05-02 so we can run the benchmark the week of 2025-05-05.
[05:23] Maya: Great. Any final questions?
[05:26] Elena: Quick question on billing proration if we start mid-month?
[05:30] Maya: We prorate committed capacity on a daily basis for partial months; i'll include a sample calculation in the amendment.
[05:36] Priya: That's helpful.
[05:38] [short pause]
[05:40] Maya: Okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. Recap of owners in meeting notes.
[05:45] Jon: Thanks all.
[05:46] Elena: Thanks.

Recap / Close:
- Renewal confirmed in principle; TerraFlux will proceed with 12-month amendment adding Dedicated EU capacity and option to convert to longer term at renewal.
- Open items: pricing amendment, SOC2/KMS docs, benchmarking plan, traffic export.
- Next milestone: send amendment by 2025-04-25; benchmark scheduled week of 2025-05-05.

References shared:
